title: Engineer zero-setup: hosted API value bites and quickstart microcopy
content:
Purpose:
Quick, portable messaging + short quickstarts aimed at engineers who value immediate results and predictable costs. This doc collects 1) tiny hero lines, 2) 30s engineer pitches, 3) two micro-quickstarts (curl + Node), 4) compact pricing anchors and billing microcopy, 5) proposed A/B tests and success criteria. Draft & iterating — lots of TODOs sprinkled.

Audience & use cases:
- Early-stage devs building prototypes or demos (fast time-to-first-LLM-response)
- Platform engineers evaluating latency/cost tradeoffs for production integration
- PMs who need a one-slide value prop for internal buy-in

Core product truths to lean on (engineering-first):
- Instant API: single API key, no infra, replies in < 100–400ms median (region-dependent) for small prompts.
- Cost controls by default: per-request token caps, auto-batching suggestions, and a clear billing preview.
- Migrate without code rewrite: same API surface for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Observability from day 0: request-level latency and cost visible in Console and SDKs.

Primary value props (short):
- Ship features, not infra — get an LLM endpoint running in minutes.
- Predictable unit economics — trade-offs you can measure, not guess.
- One API, any environment — prototype on hosted, then move to private with same calls.

Hero line candidates (one-liners for landing and CTAs):
1) "From idea to inference in under 5 minutes — one API key, no infra."
2) "Build faster: production-grade LLMs without ops overhead."
3) "Start hosted. Scale to dedicated or private with zero API changes."

30-second engineer elevator scripts (3 variants):
- Variant A (Prototype-first): "If you want a working LLM feature in minutes, Redwood’s hosted API gives you a single key, sample SDKs, and 1-click streaming. You’ll see cost and latency estimates in the Console before you hit production—so no surprise bills. If you outgrow hosted, the same API works with Dedicated or Private deployments."
- Variant B (SRE-minded): "Redwood provides production controls out of the box—per-route SLOs, rate-limits, and automatic fallbacks. You can prototype on hosted and pin the same model/rollout policy when you move to Dedicated or Private."
- Variant C (Product PM): "We reduce time-to-value by removing ops: a dev can implement a chat or summarization endpoint with a snippet and measurable cost per call. That’s faster experiments and clearer go/no-go decisions."

Quickstart microflows (short, copy-first):
- Minimal curl (one-liner emphasis):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY' \\  -d '{"model":"rwd-small-1","input":"Summarize this article in one sentence"}'
  Notes: this is the absolute minimal path to first token. Emphasize: "first response in <5 minutes from sign-up."

- Node snippet (3 lines):
  import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
  const client = new Redwood(process.env.RW_KEY);
  const res = await client.generate({model: 'rwd-small-1', input: 'Extract action items from notes'});
  Notes: include streaming example in advanced quickstart. Point to SDK repo for typed examples.

Pricing-language proposals (concise, customer-facing):
- Baseline (per-token): "Pay per token processed — transparent rates with a live cost preview in the Console. No hidden egress or compute fees."
- Starter Bundle (credit + discounted token band): "Starter: 100k tokens free credits for 30 days + discounted rate for first $50 of usage. Good for demos and low-traffic integration tests."
- Commit/Dedicated transition: "When you commit to Dedicated, you convert usage into reserved capacity with predictable monthly pricing and burst credits for spikes."

Suggested microcopy for billing screens and checkout (short):
- Checkout headline: "Projected cost: $X / 1000 calls (median payload) — adjust max_tokens to reduce price."
- Small tooltip next to model selector: "Smaller models = cheaper + faster. Choose 'rwd-small-1' for prototypes; pick 'rwd-large-1' when you need accuracy."
- Rate-limit tooltip: "Exceeding this rate will queue requests; use Dedicated for predictable throughput."

Competitive positioning bullets (how we differ, short):
- vs generic cloud provider LLM endpoints: "We provide tuned inference primitives (KV cache, batching) with developer ergonomics — not raw VM endpoints."
- vs LLM-API-only vendors: "We couple a high-throughput runtime with observability and migration paths to dedicated/private deployments."
- vs self-hosted runtimes: "No infra to own for prototyping and early-prod. When ready, move to reserved capacity without API changes."

Suggested A/B tests and metrics (quick):
- A/B headline test: "Ship features, not infra" vs "From idea to inference in 5 minutes"; metric = sign-ups started within 1 hour, and first successful API call rate.
- Pricing anchor test: per-token vs starter-bundle messaging; metric = conversion to paid within first 30 days, average spend first 90 days.
- Quickstart flow test: show 1-line curl first vs show code snippet + Console screenshot first; metric = time-to-first-request and support ticket deflection.

FAQ quick hits (for dev docs & checkout):
- Q: "What about data privacy?" A: Hosted data is encrypted in transit and at rest; options to enable private deployments and KMS/HSM for regulated workloads.
- Q: "Can I change models mid-rollout?" A: Yes — rollouts, canaries, and automatic fallback policies are first-class.
- Q: "How do I estimate cost before I build?" A: Use the Console cost preview and the SDK client-side estimator; also provide sample per-feature cost templates in docs.

Copy experiments (short snippets for email or support):
- "Prototype a smart reply in 10 minutes — try our one-liner curl and get 100k starter credits."
- "See latency & cost for each route before you deploy — prevent surprise bills."

Open questions / TODOs:
- Quantify typical latency numbers by region & model for the landing page (need SRE/benchmarks).
- Finalize exact starter credits and expiry policy (finance input needed).
- Decide whether to show "estimated cost per call" inline in code snippets (UX performance).
- Draft a short 2-screen Console tour highlighting cost preview + first API call — product to design.

Success criteria for rollout:
- 20% increase in time-to-first-successful-request (measured as sign-up -> first successful API call) within 90 days of microcopy update.
- Lower initial support questions about pricing by 30% for new sign-ups.

References / links to supporting artifacts:
- Quickstart SDK repo (linked above) and sample dashboards (see linked_artifacts).
- Bench doc TODO: /confluence/perf/hosted-latency-agg (SRE to populate).

Notes to collaborators:
- Liam: can you populate regional median latencies by model?
- Priya: finance please confirm starter credit amount and legal constraints for promos.
- Marcus: add streaming example and pick a canonical Node/Go snippet for the landing page.

This is intentionally compact — aim for a single-page landing-first copy + two quickstarts inside the docs site. Keep the hero language conversational and engineer-respecting (no fluff).

END
